```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>")
library(TALLBMDeconv)
```

The package has three modes: installed atlas, custom reference and patient-level
paired validation. Flow is optional in each. RNA composition, converted cell
proxy, and within-group expression answer different questions.

This small **synthetic software example** is not a clinical performance test.

```{r}
x <- matrix(c(20,3,6,1, 2,18,1,7, 19,4,7,2, 3,17,2,8), nrow=4)
rownames(x) <- paste0("g",1:4)
colnames(x) <- paste0("cell",1:4)
a <- data.frame(cell_id=colnames(x), group=c("A","B","A","B"))
ref <- tall_build_reference(x,a,c("donor1","donor1","donor2","donor2"),"example_v1")
bulk <- cbind(validation_patient=rowSums(x))
result <- tall_deconv(bulk,ref,config=list(iterations=400L,burnin=200L,thin=4L))
tall_extract(result)
tall_extract(result,"expression","A")
tall_qc(result)
```

For clinical deployment use the frozen default sampler configuration, unchanged
reference/gene IDs, and independently audited flow identities and denominators.
Short chains in this example only exercise the API.

`tall_benchmark` accepts a raw single-cell truth list with counts, cell_annotations
and patient_ids. It checks patient leakage, evaluates composition separately from
expression, reports missing coverage, compares expression with donor-equal reference
means, and tests patient-specific variation. Overall holdout and LOPO require
donor aggregates, not cell-level random splitting. Never call an input flow gate
an independent composition validation.

The full atlas deployment resource and the benchmark73 resource have distinct
IDs. The former does not inherit the latter's heldout accuracy. See the README
for installation, permission status, all scales, flow schemas and frozen settings.
